chapter: Asides on character, a piano and Oslo
title: The pianist imposed on him in Oslo
summary: Briggs usually chose his own men, but at the Hotel Bristol in Oslo the proprietor imposed a poor South African pianist who tried to get the band thrown out and was himself deported.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: And my relationships in general, just as I've told you, most of the orchestras I've had, have been, I select the men myself.
Right.
And I did not accept a job if the proprietor tried to tell me to take so and so, and so and so.
Right.

It happened just once to me, way back in London, when I went to Oslo. The proprietor of the Hotel Bristol, Mr. Jensen, imposed a pianist on me. That was okay, it didn't make any difference. But this person, it so happened he was a, he was not a genial person.
Right.
We went to Oslo and I don't generally criticize musicians 'cause I feel if you're good, you're okay, and if you're not good, you have to live. You see, that's the way I've always been. You
Briggs
maybe don't make the grade but you have to live as a human being, and if you try your best, you're okay.
Well, this guy, as far as I'm concerned, he was really the world's worst pianist.
Really.
(Laughter). He couldn't read, he couldn't play. He was never an instrumentalist. He never studied, and he knew nothing about the instrument.

But the worst thing about him is this -- I don't like to say things like this, but I have to tell you this. I realized and found out that he was from South Africa, and that was the cause of everything.
I see, sure.
That was the background---of everything.
So, finally I mentioned something -- did you read about Oslo?
Briggs
Yes.
Well, you see, what happened, he did everything to have us thrown out. We were not thrown out. We finished our contracts.
And he had arranged to replace us, have men come in, but he -- he was thrown out of the country. He was thrown out of the country: He was deported.
Yes, yes. Well, I guess --
I don't care about that. I don't judge anyone.
Right. Well, I guess that's the important thing.
